description: Signature edition. overview: In the Signature teaching of home brew safety, What Home Brew Safety Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Sanitization vs cleaning means cleaning removes grime, sanitizing kills microbes; both are required Complete fermentation means bottling active ferment causes gushers or bursting bottles Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Sanitization vs cleaning: cleaning removes grime, sanitizing kills microbes; both are required
Complete fermentation: bottling active ferment causes gushers or bursting bottles
key_laws: Sanitize everything that touches the brew after the boil; this prevents nearly all failures.
vocabulary: Infection: wild microbes souring or ruining a batch, almost always from poor sanitation
Bottle bomb: a bottle bursting from excess pressure, dangerous and preventable
methods: Sanitize method: clean with a brewery wash, rinse, soak in no-rinse sanitizer for the contact time, air dry
